findings.title: Heart-rate alert shows clock time only
findings.description: `_caregiver_message` formats heart-rate timestamps with `%H:%M` instead of `_utc_text`, omitting the date and timezone and bypassing UTC conversion. When a heart-rate reading has a valid non-UTC timestamp, the message contains only its local clock time, and the CLI presents that message directly to the caregiver.

findings.title: Escalation set outside the rules engine
findings.description: `HealthSentinel.assess` ORs `decision.requires_escalation` with a hard-coded `reading.values.get("bpm", 0) > 150` check, allowing the agent to override its supplied ruleset. With a ruleset whose red cutoff is above 155 bpm, a 155 bpm reading can be classified amber but still marked for escalation under that ruleset's version label; a missing `bpm` key defaults to 0 and silently bypasses the check.

citations.citation: Only the rules or baseline modules may decide triage and escalation

- **Rules decide triage, the LLM only explains it.** Only `core/rules` sets `triage` or
  `requires_escalation`. Code in `agents/` reads the decision and never changes it.

## Product decisions to respect
- **Rules decide triage, the LLM only explains it.** Only `core/rules` sets `triage` or
  `requires_escalation`. Code in `agents/` reads the decision and never changes it.
- **A model outage must never hide an alert.** Every model call has a timeout, a template

evidence.explanation: The agent accepts a RuleSet and uses the engine's decision for triage, but the added expression in `agents/health_sentinel/agent.py` computes escalation using a separate fixed threshold. The checklist and REVIEW.md require core/rules to decide escalation. The shipped red cutoff of greater than 130 bpm means the disagreement appears with a different supplied ruleset, such as one that returns amber at 155 bpm.

findings.title: Health readings are written to logs
findings.description: `HealthSentinel.assess` passes `reading.elder_id` and the complete `reading.values` dictionary to `logger.info`, exposing heart-rate or blood-pressure measurements alongside the elder ID. This runs on every assessment, including those that return green, and sends those details to the application log stream for anyone with log access to read.

findings.title: Message test no longer checks the time
findings.description: `test_heart_rate_full_result` replaces its exact caregiver-message assertion with a check that only distinguishes `None` from non-`None`. For amber and red readings, the test now accepts any string, so it misses changes to the measurement, date, UTC timestamp, and triage text, including the clock-only regression.

findings.title: Test suite now needs internet access
findings.description: `test_can_reach_example_host` uses `socket.create_connection` to open a real TCP connection to `example.com:443` instead of testing an isolated component. Because the ordinary `make test` run collects it, local and CI runs without outbound connectivity can fail or wait for a connection timeout.
